solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old age turning round stone trail

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another
something turning faces the other way, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: ELD is an archaic word for old age
RAGG (or rag) is a hard coarse stone, as in ragstone

explanation.surface: An ancient person shuffling slowly around a stone on a path.
explanation.walkthrough: ELD is a Mephisto staple for old age; reversed it wraps round RAGG, the Chambers spelling of the coarse stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To draggle is to trail along the ground and so become wet and muddy, as a long skirt does.

clue.text: Drum and bass hosted by deejay Earl and myself

indicators.note: a host has a guest inside the house, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: a deejay is a DJ
E is the abbreviation for earl
the setter refers to himself as ME
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: Drum and bass music being played by a DJ who is also a nobleman, with the setter joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drum and bass' reads as the music genre, but the drum is the definition and bass is just B, tucked inside ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A djembe is a goblet-shaped West African hand drum played with bare hands.

clue.text: Cracked urinal — time for new lavabo?

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are reassembled
one thing standing for another means it takes the other's place, so one letter is swapped in

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
N is the abbreviation for new; it is the letter that goes out

explanation.surface: A broken urinal suggests it is time to buy a new washbasin.
explanation.walkthrough: Lavabo looks like a plain washbasin, which suits the surface, but here it is the priest's ceremonial hand-washing at Mass; T replaces N in URINAL before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The lavabo is a ceremonial washing of the celebrant's hands during Mass, so it is an example of a ritual.

clue.text: One tweeting "fleet's passing close to war". Keir

indicators.note: passing something up means doing without it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word, which is removed
a keir (or kier) is a vat used for bleaching cloth

explanation.surface: A tweet about a navy approaching war, signed off by a politician named Keir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keir' masquerades as the Prime Minister signing off a tweet, but it is a Chambers word for a bleaching tub.
explanation.definitionFit: The amadavat, or avadavat, is a small red Indian waxbill finch kept as a cage songbird, and birds tweet.

clue.text: Doctor having yen to enter historic hall

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to doctor an animal is to neuter it, i.e. geld it
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A physician with a longing to visit an old stately hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician but is the verb meaning to castrate; 'yen' looks like a craving but is the currency symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyeld is Spenser's old spelling of guild, used for a guildhall, so it is an obsolete word for such a building.

clue.text: Very elf-shot as these hit?

indicators.note: something hit is knocked about, so these letters are jolted into a new order

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone struck so suddenly they seem bewitched by fairy arrows.
explanation.walkthrough: Elf-shot means struck by an elf's arrow, hence bewitched; the whole clue describes the victim of Cupid's darts while also supplying the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-shafts are Cupid's arrows, and anyone they strike is smitten as if shot by a fairy, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Oriental jacket and trousers together with short coat

indicators.note: something short lacks its full length, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: SAM is an old Spenserian word meaning together
a fur is a coat; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A description of an Eastern outfit: a jacket and trousers worn with a short coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together' reads as part of the clothing description but is the archaic SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A samfu is a Chinese outfit of a loose jacket worn over matching trousers, traditionally by women.

clue.text: Largely flatter in truth

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to soothe is to flatter or cajole

explanation.surface: Mostly flattering someone while telling the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flatter' looks like a comparative adjective but is the verb, as in to soothe someone's ego.
explanation.definitionFit: Sooth is an old word for truth or reality, surviving in 'in sooth' and 'soothsayer'.

clue.text: One missing being moved into a labour co-operative?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: a bee is a gathering of neighbours working together, as in a quilting bee
sent means moved emotionally, transported

explanation.surface: A missing person who has been relocated to a workers' collective.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee, chiefly in North America, is a social gathering where people pool their labour on one task.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is not present where expected, such as at work or school.

clue.text: Fivers on floor hide boot

parts.note: a fin is US slang for a five-dollar bill
to floor someone is to knock them out, a KO

explanation.surface: Banknotes left on the floor hidden inside a boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb about concealing cash, but it is leather, qualifying the boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A finsko is a Lapp boot made of reindeer skin with the fur on, so a footwear item of animal leather.

clue.text: Early signs of lung pain not appearing as unpleasant as before

indicators.note: early signs are the opening letters, which are the ones affected here
what does not appear is left out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the word without its first letter
the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: First symptoms of lung pain failing to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks the definition as an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungain is an obsolete word meaning inconvenient or troublesome, the root of the surviving word ungainly.

clue.text: Pound joint with intramuscular protein pushing top of leg back

parts.note: J is an abbreviation for joint

indicators.note: shoving the opening letter of the limb further along reorders the word, though only that single letter changes place

parts.note: IM is the medical abbreviation for intramuscular
myoglobin is the oxygen-carrying protein in muscle

explanation.surface: A medical note about a battered joint and a muscle protein shifting the upper leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushing top of leg back' moves the L of MYOGLOBIN one place later. Jimmy o'goblin is rhyming slang for sovereign, the pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy o'goblin is Cockney rhyming slang for a sovereign, a gold coin worth one pound sterling.

clue.text: Character facing exhaustion spread over a day's march

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the letters run the other way
the character at the face of a word is its front letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
pâté is a spread for toast

explanation.surface: Someone close to collapse from tiredness after a long day's walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person, but here it means a letter, the one at the face of 'exhaustion'; that letter and the spread are then turned round together.
explanation.definitionFit: An étape is a military term for a day's march, or the stopping place at the end of one.

clue.text: Preparing element of script to be injected?

definitions.text: Preparing element of script to be injected?

indicators.note: an injected thing goes inside, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: doing, as in doing the vegetables, means preparing

indicators.note: an element is one component, here the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nurse readying a prescribed drug for an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: A script is informal for a prescription, so the whole clue also describes giving medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosing is giving a patient measured amounts of medicine, which is what preparing a prescribed injection amounts to.

clue.text: Pen erred so suspect Milton's blindness?

indicators.note: something suspect is not what it seems, so these letters hide their true order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer's errors make us wonder whether Milton's blindness was to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton, who went blind, used the term in Paradise Lost; it translates the Latin gutta serena.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop serene is Milton's rendering of gutta serena, an old medical name for the type of blindness he suffered.

clue.text: One scrambling racehorse liking heavy going crossing line

indicators.note: to cross something is to lie across it, so one piece straddles the other

parts.note: a mudder is a horse that runs well on soft, muddy ground
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A horse that loves soft ground scrambling across the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambling' suggests a horse struggling in the race, but it means jumbling things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddler is someone who muddles, mixing things into confusion, just as scrambling jumbles them.

clue.text: Old savings account's funds possibly doubling

indicators.note: doubling back means retracing your route, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: funds are an example of an asset

explanation.surface: Money in an old savings account possibly doubling in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubling' looks like money growing, but it means doubling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A TESSA was a Tax Exempt Special Savings Account, a UK scheme running from 1991 until replaced by ISAs in 1999.

clue.text: Overture from troubador in verse performing?

definitions.text: Overture from troubador in verse performing?

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces in a new routine
an overture opens a piece, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wandering minstrel opening his act with a song in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a piece a troubadour would perform in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sirvente is a medieval Provençal poem or lay, often satirical, composed and sung by troubadours.

clue.text: Whip cape off Native American

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of kilter, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to snatch a cloak away from a Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' and 'off' read as one phrasal verb, but 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chippewa, also called Ojibwe, are a large Indigenous people of the Great Lakes region of North America.

clue.text: Mischievous Costello maybe, "What's on second?"

indicators.note: one piece placed on another follows it in the answer

parts.note: Elvis Costello is an English singer-songwriter

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the word

parts.note: the letter in position two of the word

explanation.surface: A play on Abbott and Costello's comedy routine 'Who's on first?', with a cheeky Costello.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Lou Costello of Abbott and Costello, whose sketch asks who is on first base; the Costello wanted is the singer Elvis.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvish means like an elf, and elves are traditionally impish, so the word carries the sense of playfully naughty.

clue.text: Sybil perhaps one of Cleese's creations?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prophetess or soothsaying spirit, like the oracle at Delphi
second meaning: a member of the comedy team John Cleese co-founded

explanation.surface: Is Sybil one of the characters John Cleese invented?
explanation.walkthrough: Sybil Fawlty, the wife in Cleese's sitcom Fawlty Towers, makes the surface ring true; the spelling also suggests a sibyl, a prophetess.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chambers a python is a soothsaying spirit or a person possessed by one, and each member of Monty Python co-created the show with Cleese.

clue.text: Spinning wheel to scorch statue of one departed

parts.note: to char is to scorch
in Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spirit double, also a statue of the dead person in the tomb

explanation.surface: Using a spinning wheel to burn a memorial statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The KA is a Mephisto favourite from Egyptian religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A charka, or charkha, is the Indian domestic spinning wheel championed by Gandhi.

clue.text: Caravan shaft once locked by drive in Scotland

indicators.note: something locked by another is held fast inside it, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: CA' or CAA is Scots for to drive or push
FIL is a Shakespearean word for the shaft of a cart

explanation.surface: An old caravan's shaft jammed while being driven in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caravan' suggests a trailer, but the answer is the older sense of a group of travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafila is a caravan in the sense of a company of travellers or train of camels crossing a desert.

clue.text: Boycott in India almost fit retaining technique

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece holds the other inside
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: hale means healthy and fit
an art is a skill or technique

explanation.surface: A boycott in India that nearly failed but kept its methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like a noun or verb about suitability, but it is the adjective for healthy; the shortening happens before the technique goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hartal is a mass closure of shops and businesses in South Asia as a political protest, a form of boycott or strike.

clue.text: First product in smelting delivered tincture

indicators.note: a delivered speech is spoken out, so we go by how the word is said

parts.note: a spice is a tincture in the sense of a trace or touch of something

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: the first thing smelting produced was a tincture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tincture' here is not a medicine but a slight flavour or trace, which is one sense of spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Speiss is a mixture of metallic arsenides and antimonides formed as an early by-product when smelting certain ores.

clue.text: Izzard appearing in sleek dicky, one from Transylvania

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be found inside it, so one piece sits within the other
dicky means shaky or unsound, so these letters are unsteady and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
izzard is an old name for the letter Z

explanation.surface: The comedian Eddie Izzard turning up in a smart outfit as a Transylvanian.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddie Izzard is the surface's comedian, but izzard is a dialect name for the letter Z; 'dicky' is British for unsound or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: The Szekely, singular Szekel, are a Hungarian-speaking people living in eastern Transylvania in Romania.

clue.text: Both sides of single covering Mud recalled jazzer's style

indicators.note: a cover goes round what it covers, so one piece wraps the other
the two sides of a word are its edges, so only its outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the opening and closing letters of the word

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: mud is dirt

explanation.surface: A jazz musician recalling a single cover version by the 1970s glam band Mud.
explanation.walkthrough: Mud was a British glam-rock band, which suits 'single' and 'covering' in the surface; here it is just dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Stride is a jazz piano style in which the left hand leaps between bass notes and chords.

clue.text: Earthenware container having fruit cut from garcinia tree

indicators.note: something cut from a whole is removed from it, leaving the remainder

parts.note: the mangosteen is a tropical tree of the genus Garcinia
a mango is a fruit; it is the part removed

explanation.surface: A clay pot holding fruit trimmed from a tropical tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Garcinia is the botanical genus of the mangosteen; taking out the fruit leaves the tail of the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A steen, or stean, is an old dialect word for a large earthenware jar or vessel.

clue.text: Hindu festival motions Indian ascetic dropping in

parts.note: motions are bowel movements, i.e. poo

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: a Jain follows an Indian religion known for asceticism
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Proposals at a Hindu festival as a holy man drops by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motions' reads as formal proposals or gestures, but it is the medical sense of bowel movements.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooja, or puja, is Hindu worship and also names festivals of worship such as Durga Puja.

clue.text: Omen's following a little tetchy after part of film's cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the last letter goes
one piece coming after another is placed later in the answer

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following
a film is stored on reels; the last letter goes

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small bit of it, here the opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ominous sign follows when a slightly irritable director cuts part of the film.
explanation.walkthrough: The order matters: the trimmed reel comes before the letter from 'tetchy', and F leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Freet, or freit, is a Scots word for an omen or superstitious sign.

clue.text: Stalwart actor, curt unpleasant sort, to perform without cast

indicators.note: curt means cut short, so the final letter is lost
without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: an old trout is a disagreeable person, usually an old woman
taken as written
a cast is a mould or form; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A brusque, disagreeable actor having to go on without the rest of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as the actors in a play but means a mould, a form.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouper is an experienced, dependable performer, and by extension anyone who perseveres without complaint.

clue.text: Auntie's releasing advanced new music app

indicators.note: a new version is remade, so these letters take a different order
releasing something lets it go, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level; it is removed

explanation.surface: The BBC, nicknamed Auntie, launching a new music app.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC, which fits a story about releasing an app.
explanation.definitionFit: iTunes is Apple's software and store for buying, playing and organising digital music.

clue.text: One wrestling attention seeker nicking Russian con

indicators.note: nicking means grabbing hold of, so one piece is seized inside the other

parts.note: 'Oi!' is a call used to get someone's attention
a zek was a prisoner in a Soviet labour camp

explanation.surface: An attention-hungry wrestler arresting a Russian convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' is short for convict, and the Soviet-era slang for one is a three-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozeki is the second-highest rank in professional sumo, so an ozeki is a high-ranking wrestler.

clue.text: Want learned judge to be cast hollow-faced?

indicators.note: metal that is cast is melted and remoulded, so these letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: Wanting a scholarly judge with a gaunt face to be cast in a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' fits the casting of a part in the surface, but it signals the letters being remoulded.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantern-jawed describes a long thin face with a protruding jaw and sunken cheeks, so gaunt or sunken-cheeked.

clue.text: Uncovered striking offensive

indicators.note: uncovering strips off an outer layer, so the outermost letters are removed

parts.note: salient means striking or prominent

explanation.walkthrough: 'striking offensive' reads like a military attack, but the words split into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien can mean repugnant or contrary to someone's nature, as in cruelty being alien to her, hence distasteful.

clue.text: Edible marine plant boiled as a leek

indicators.note: boiled food is broken down and churned about, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaside vegetable that is cooked like a leek.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: the blanched shoots of this coastal plant are boiled and eaten like asparagus or leeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea kale is a cabbage-family plant of coastal shingle whose young shoots are eaten as a vegetable.
